title: Shrinking a section pencil to a finite surjective morphism
statement:
Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K$, put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and fix $s\in U$. Let $p:Y\to U$ be proper. Let $B$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $\alpha,\beta\in\Gamma(Y,B)$ ordinary global sections. Assume their restrictions generate $B_s$ on $Y_s$ and define a finite morphism $\psi_s:Y_s\to\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. Assume their restrictions also generate $B_K$ and define a finite surjective morphism $\psi_K:Y_K\to\mathbf P^1_K$. Then there is an affine open neighbourhood $U'\subseteq U$ of $s$ such that $\alpha,\beta$ generate $B$ on $Y_{U'}$ and define a finite surjective morphism $\psi:Y_{U'}\to\mathbf P^1_{U'}$ whose restrictions to $s$ and $K$ are the specified morphisms. If a group acts on $Y$ over $U$ and the section morphism is invariant on the open locus where $\alpha,\beta$ generate, its restriction $\psi$ is invariant as well. If the specified $\psi_K$ is etale on a nonempty open, this same generic-fibre assertion holds for $\psi$.

Proper morphisms, invertible modules, scheme fibres, base change, generating sections, their projective-coordinate morphisms, finite and surjective morphisms and etale morphisms are [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-sc-invertible-module], [def-pc-scheme-fibre], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], [def-weil-pbc-morphism-to-projective-space-by-sections], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A Noetherian ring means one in which every ideal is finitely generated; an integral domain has $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors.

proof.text: Let $W=Y_\alpha\cup Y_\beta$, where $Y_\alpha$ and $Y_\beta$ are the nonvanishing opens of the sections. The nonvanishing lemma makes $W$ open, and the fibre criterion says that the sections generate $B|_W$. Every point $y$ over $s$ belongs to $W$: the value of a pulled-back section in $B_s\otimes\kappa(y)$ is its original value in $B\otimes\kappa(y)$, by associativity of tensor products, and the sections generate on $Y_s$. The same holds over the generic point by the generic generation assumption. Thus $Z=Y\setminus W$ is closed and disjoint from both fibres. Properness of $p$ means in particular that it is a closed map, so $p(Z)$ is closed and misses $s$. Choose a principal open $V=D(a)\subseteq U\setminus p(Z)$ containing $s$. Such a principal open exists by the basis of the topology of $\operatorname{Spec}A$; $a\notin\mathfrak p_s$ implies $a\ne0$, so $V$ also contains the generic point. We have $Y_V\subseteq W$ and the two sections generate there.

source.place: Tag 01CY, lemma-s-open; Tag 01AM, generation; morphisms.tex Tag 01W1, definition-proper. Agent closed-base-locus argument for de Jong §3.4, p.606.

proof.text: The generating pair on $Y_V$ defines a $V$-morphism $h:Y_V\to P=\mathbf P^1_V$ by the projective-coordinate construction. Its restrictions to $s$ and $K$ are exactly $\psi_s$ and $\psi_K$: the projective-space functor-of-points statement is compatible with pullback, and the relative morphism is the unique map with this absolute projective-coordinate map and the prescribed base projection. This also identifies every subsequent base restriction with the morphism defined by the restricted sections.

source.place: Tag 01NE, lemma-projective-space, and the relative morphism paragraph following definition-projective-space (01NF).

proof.text: The morphism $p_V:Y_V\to V$ is proper by base change. The projective-space structural map $q:P\to V$ is proper, hence separated. Apply the proper-over-separated lemma to $p_V=q\circ h$ to conclude that $h$ is proper. In particular its finite-fibre neighbourhood theorem applies, without any flatness hypothesis on $Y/V$.

source.place: Tags 01W4, lemma-base-change-proper, and 01W6, lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed (2); constructions.tex Tag 01NH and projective-space properness.

proof.text: For each point $t\in P_s$, write $\bar t$ for its image in $P$. The fibre projection identifies $P_s$ with the subspace $q^{-1}(s)$ and identifies $\kappa(t)$ with $\kappa(\bar t)$: base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ does not change the residue field of a point lying over $s$. The two fibre products $Y_s\times_{P_s}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $Y_V\times_P\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\bar t)$ are therefore canonically isomorphic by the universal property. Thus $h^{-1}(\{\bar t\})$ is finite since $\psi_s$ is finite. The proper finite-fibre neighbourhood lemma gives an open $O_t\subseteq P$ containing $\bar t$ on which $h$ is finite. Put $O=\bigcup_{t\in P_s}O_t$. Then $O$ contains $q^{-1}(s)$, and finiteness local on the target shows that $h^{-1}(O)\to O$ is finite, including when some of the fibres are empty.

source.place: Tag 02UP, lemma-proper-finite-fibre-finite-in-neighbourhood; morphisms.tex Tags 01WI, lemma-finite-local, and 02NH, finite fibres.

proof.text: The complement $P\setminus O$ is closed. Since $q$ is proper, $q(P\setminus O)$ is closed in $V$ and misses $s$. Choose $b\in A$ with $s\in U'=D(b)\subseteq V\setminus q(P\setminus O)$, using the principal-open basis of $U$. Then $b\ne0$, this open is affine, and its generic point still has residue field $K$. The open immersion $\mathbf P^1_{U'}=q^{-1}(U')\to P$ has image in $O$, so it factors uniquely through the open subscheme $O$ by restriction of the structure sheaf. Base-changing the finite map $h^{-1}(O)\to O$ along this factorization gives the finite map $\psi:Y_{U'}\to\mathbf P^1_{U'}$, by the fibre-product universal property. Generation and both specified fibre identifications persist from steps 1 and 2.

source.place: Tags 01W1, definition-proper, and 01WL, lemma-base-change-finite; agent base shrinking of the target neighbourhoods from 02UP.

proof.text: The generic fibre $\mathbf P^1_K$ is dense in $\mathbf P^1_{U'}$. Indeed the standard-chart statement covers the latter by two copies of $\operatorname{Spec}(A_b[T])$, with their indicated base projections. Each chart ring is an integral domain: the highest nonzero coefficients of two nonzero polynomials have nonzero product, and localization at $b\ne0$ preserves a domain. Its zero ideal is prime, belongs to every nonempty basic open $D(f)$, and contracts to the zero ideal in $A_b$. Thus it is a point of the generic fibre and every nonempty open of either chart meets that fibre. Since the two charts cover, the generic fibre is dense in the whole projective line.

source.place: Tag 01NG, lemma-standard-covering-projective-space; elementary polynomial-domain and basic-open argument.

proof.text: The image of $\psi$ is closed because $\psi$ is finite. It contains the image of the generic pencil, which is all of $\mathbf P^1_K$ by hypothesis and step 2. By the density in step 6, the image is all of $\mathbf P^1_{U'}$. This proves surjectivity in the sense of the surjective-morphism definition.

source.place: Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper; closed image containing a dense subset.

proof.text: If the additional group hypothesis holds, the invariant section morphism $h_W:W\to\mathbf P^1_U$ on the generation locus $W$ restricts to $\psi$ on $Y_{U'}\subseteq W$: the projective-coordinate morphism is compatible with pullback along the open immersion $Y_{U'}\to W$, so $h_W|_{Y_{U'}}$ has the base projection of $Y_{U'}$ and the projective-coordinate map of the restricted pair $\alpha,\beta$, hence equals $\psi$ by the uniqueness in the relative construction. Every group element acts over $U$, so preserves $Y_{U'}$; restricting the assumed equality $h_W\circ g=h_W$ gives $\psi\circ g|_{Y_{U'}}=\psi$. Finally $\psi_K$ is the original generic-fibre morphism by step 2. Any nonempty open of $Y_K$ on which that original morphism is etale is therefore the very same open with the very same morphism for the final pencil, proving the last assertion.

source.place: Tag 01NE, pullback compatibility; elementary restriction of the assumed invariance and generic-fibre equality in de Jong §3.4.
